title: std/media-asset@1
description: A video asset, in both directions: on the way in, `uri` names where the source can be fetched; on the way out, `uri` is the address of the packaged result. Deliberately NOT std/document@1: a video is named by an envelope rather than carried in one — an hour of it is gigabytes, and the packaged form is a tree of playlists and segments rather than a blob. Everything but `uri` is optional, because the ingress side of an edge knows almost nothing and the egress side knows all of it.

uri.description: Where the media is. Inbound: a source the media subsystem can fetch. Outbound: the address of the HLS master playlist.

mime.description: Media type of the source, when the sender knows it.

asset_id.description: The media subsystem's id for this asset, so a consumer can ask it directly afterwards.

state.description: Outbound only. `ready` is the only state in which `uri` is fetchable.

renditions.description: The ladder that was encoded, tallest first.

frames.description: Addresses of still frames sampled from the source, in time order. Every capability that reasons about video needs frames, and they come out of the decode the encode already did.

poster.description: Address of a single representative frame.

error.description: Why it failed, in the words of whoever has to act on it. Present only with state `failed`.
